briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
A potential framework agreement between the United States and Iran is nearing finalization, primarily focusing on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, easing sanctions, and a ceasefire across regional fronts, but with significant disagreements remaining over Iran's nuclear program and the scope of its sovereign control. Concurrently, the northern Israel-Lebanon border continues to experience drone and rocket attacks, resulting in an Israeli casualty, while Israeli forces continue operations in central Gaza.

IRAN
Iran executed Mojtaba Kalan today, after he was convicted of providing intelligence to Israel and the US during the recent war. Negotiations for a potential memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the US are reportedly in their final stages, with Pakistan and Qatar acting as mediators. A senior Iranian official stated to Reuters that Tehran will not agree to hand over its highly enriched uranium, and that the nuclear issue is not part of the preliminary agreement. Tasnim News Agency reported a 60-day period for nuclear talks, with Iran having agreed to nothing in this domain so far. However, an Axios report suggests the MoU draft includes Iran's commitment to never seek nuclear weapons and to negotiate the suspension of uranium enrichment and removal of highly enriched uranium.

On the Strait of Hormuz, while the proposed MoU aims to reopen it for free passage, Iran's Fars News Agency denies claims by US President Trump that it would revert to pre-war status, asserting Iran will retain control over passage routes, timing, and permits, with only traffic volume returning to previous levels. Hussein Shariatmadari, editor of Keyhan newspaper, stressed Iran's legal right to collect transit fees for the strait as its territorial water. Regarding sanctions and assets, Iranian sources demand the immediate release of a specified portion of frozen funds as a prerequisite for the agreement. The New York Times reported the agreement could release $25 billion in frozen assets, but major releases would be contingent on a final nuclear deal.

Internally, Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf has been authorized by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei to make decisions regarding the agreement. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Commander-in-Chief Ahmad Vahidi declared Iran emerged victorious from the "Third Imposed War" (US-Israeli terrorist attack) and emphasized reliance on internal strength and active deterrence, stating Iran's armed forces are at the "highest level of readiness." President Pezeshkian emphasized national unity and adherence to the Supreme National Security Council decisions, with the Supreme Leader's permission. Economically, high gasoline prices in the US, linked to Hormuz disruptions, are seen as a challenge for the Trump administration. FIFA has approved Iran's national football team's request to switch its 2026 World Cup training base from Arizona to Tijuana, Mexico, citing visa and national airline use advantages.

ISRAEL
Sgt. Noam Hamburger, 23, from Atlit, a combatant in technology and maintenance, was killed in operational activity in northern Israel. An additional soldier was seriously injured, and an NCO lightly injured in the same incident, caused by an explosive drone. Earlier, two men, approximately 50 years old, died following a light aircraft crash in the Jezreel Valley near Tel Adashim.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) reported multiple hostile aircraft intrusion alerts in northern Israel (e.g., Idmit, Arab al-Aramshe, Shomera, Even Menachem, Rosh HaNikra, Metulla), some involving suspicious aerial targets and others later identified as false alarms. The IDF also conducted a military exercise along the northern coastline, involving drones. The Home Front Command's defensive policy remains unchanged until 26 May 2026, 20:00 UTC.

Prime Minister Netanyahu condemned the shooting near the White House and referred to President Trump as "the best friend Israel ever had in the White House." A senior Israeli political source indicated that the US is updating Israel on the Hormuz MoU, and Netanyahu stressed Israel's right to freedom of action in all arenas, including Lebanon, a principle backed by Trump. Netanyahu is scheduled to convene the "mini-cabinet" and coalition and opposition faction heads tonight to discuss developments with Iran. Israeli officials have expressed concerns that US envoy Steve Witkoff is pushing for an agreement "at any cost." An American soldier in the Israeli Army, Alex Miller, 23, reportedly committed suicide in the US after returning from Gaza due to severe psychological trauma. Five Israeli civilians crossed into Lebanon and were returned by the IDF and arrested.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces in the Southern Command attacked and destroyed three Hamas weapons depots in central Gaza in the past 24 hours, uncovering anti-tank rockets, RPGs, explosives, and other combat gear. Secondary explosions were observed after the strikes. Separately, there were reports of several casualties from an Israeli bombardment of a residential building in Deir Al-Balah, central Gaza. The Palestinian resistance movement Hamas condemned Israeli strikes on police stations as an attempt to create a "security vacuum." Palestinians in Gaza are reportedly barred from Hajj amid Israeli restrictions. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers allegedly attempted to burn down a mosque during an assault on the town of Kifl Haris.

LEBANON
Hezbollah continued cross-border operations, claiming drone attacks against Israeli military targets. Specific incidents cited include targeting Israeli "Nemira" vehicles at Khallat al-Raj in Deir Siryan (18 & 21 May), in Hadatha (20 May), in Taybe (16 May), and a HIMAT logistical vehicle at the Manara site (04 May), all with Ababil drones. An Ababil drone was also reportedly used against the 300th Brigade commander's vehicle in Shomera base (18 May).

In response, Israeli forces reportedly launched airstrikes on the towns of Jibshit and Yaroun a-Shaqif in southern Lebanon. An Israeli drone strike was reported to have hit a vehicle in Zefta. The IDF also announced the destruction of a 100-meter long underground tunnel route in southern Lebanon. Lebanese official sources indicated that Lebanon has not yet received official information regarding the implications of a potential Iran-US agreement on the Lebanese front but welcomes any accord leading to a full cessation of hostilities in Lebanon. Two Israeli soldiers were moderately and lightly injured by an explosive drone in southern Lebanon; this is believed to be the same incident that killed Sgt. Noam Hamburger.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Iraq's Counter-Terrorism Service announced the martyrdom of 3 fighters and injury of 4 others due to an ISIS ordnance explosion in the Hatra desert, Ninawa province. A landmine explosion in Tayeb, Maysan, initially killed one person. Iraqi Joint Operations Command stated F-16 airstrikes successfully targeted an ISIS hideout in Wadi al-Shay, Kirkuk, killing 4 terrorists.

In northern Iraq, explosions were reported in Samawa, Tarmia (Baghdad's north), Erbil, and Sulaymaniyah. Reports indicated a rocket attack on the headquarters of the opposition Freedom Party in Erbil, with US warplanes flying over Khelifan in Erbil. Iranian sources also reported IRGC attacks on Kurdistan Region bases in Erbil. The US Secretary of Defense alluded to plans to deploy airborne and rapid reaction forces to the Middle East, including HIMARS systems, to protect US bases and personnel from Iranian proxies, signaling a readiness to counter proxy activities in the region. Armed groups affiliated with the Iranian opposition (Yekiti and Komala) reportedly imposed a military cordon around the Surin Mountains in Sulaymaniyah.

GULF STATES
President Trump engaged in extensive phone consultations with leaders from Saudi Arabia (Mohammed bin Salman), UAE (Mohammed bin Zayed), Qatar (Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani), Turkey (Recep Tayyip Erdogan), Egypt (Abdel Fattah el-Sisi), Jordan (King Abdullah II), and Bahrain (King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa), concerning the potential Iran-US peace memorandum of understanding. Regional leaders reportedly expressed support for advancing a deal to end the war and de-escalate tensions. Qatar's Emir emphasized the Gulf State's consistent stance on prioritizing peaceful solutions and supporting all initiatives aimed at de-escalation. Pakistan's Foreign Minister also noted Trump's outreach as a significant step towards regional peace. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in a meeting with India's Prime Minister, asserted that the United States would "not allow Iran to hold the global energy market hostage" in the Strait of Hormuz, highlighting a key US concern for the region's economy. Bahrain's most prominent Shia cleric criticized hawkish US policies toward Iran, affirming Iran's right to self-defense, with chants of "Labaik Khamenei" reported in Manama despite government bans on mourning processions.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Imminent Iran-US Framework Agreement:** The United States and Iran are reportedly close to finalizing a 60-day memorandum of understanding (MoU), referred to by some as the 'Islamabad Declaration,' mediated by Pakistan and Qatar, aiming to de-escalate regional tensions.
2.  **Strait of Hormuz Reopening & Sanctions Relief:** The proposed MoU includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz for free passage, with Iran asserting continued sovereign control over management and permits, and the temporary lifting of the US naval blockade and some oil sanctions, with promises of releasing $25 billion to several billion in frozen Iranian assets.
3.  **Nuclear Program Remains Contentious:** While the MoU aims for a ceasefire and de-escalation, the core issue of Iran's nuclear program, particularly its highly enriched uranium stockpile, is largely deferred to subsequent 30-60 day negotiations, with Iran explicitly stating it will not concede on this in the initial phase.
4.  **Israeli Casualty in Northern Conflict:** Sgt. Noam Hamburger, 23, from Atlit, a combatant in technology and maintenance, was killed in operational activity in northern Israel due to an explosive drone. Two other soldiers were injured in the same incident.
5.  **Ongoing Hostilities on Israel-Lebanon Border:** Numerous hostile aircraft intrusion alerts were triggered in northern Israel (e.g., Idmit, Shomera, Metulla), some involving suspicious aerial targets, others deemed false alarms. Hezbollah claimed multiple drone attacks against Israeli military targets in southern Lebanon.
6.  **Washington White House Shooting:** A 21-year-old individual, Nasire Best, with a history of mental issues, was fatally shot by the US Secret Service near the White House after opening fire. A bystander was also injured.
7.  **Iran Executes Alleged Spy:** Iran announced the execution of Mojtaba Kalan, convicted of providing intelligence to Israel and the US during the recent war.
8.  **Major Russian Offensive in Ukraine:** Russia launched a massive "revenge" attack on Ukraine, including 90 missiles and 600 drones, using advanced hypersonic "Zircon" and ballistic "Oreshnik" missiles. Ukraine claims to have intercepted 55 missiles and 549 drones.
9.  **US Military Posture:** The US Secretary of Defense alluded to plans to deploy rapid reaction forces to the Middle East, including HIMARS systems, to protect US bases and personnel from Iranian proxies, signaling a readiness to counter proxy activities in the region.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high, especially concerning the implementation details of the potential Iran-US MoU, given conflicting claims of sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz and the deferment of critical nuclear issues. The Israel-Lebanon border is an active flashpoint, with continued cross-border drone and rocket attacks, exemplified by the death of an Israeli soldier. In Iraq, persistent reports of explosions and attacks attributed to various groups suggest ongoing instability. Iranian military leadership explicitly states its forces are at the "highest level of readiness," warning of a "devastating and hellish response" to renewed aggression, while the US is reportedly preparing rapid reaction forces for deployment, indicating a readiness for military engagement. US red lines include the full dismantling of Iran's nuclear program and free passage through Hormuz, while Iran's red lines include non-negotiation of nuclear details in the initial phase and affirmation of sovereign control over the Strait. Israel maintains its red line of freedom of action against threats in all arenas, including Lebanon, and preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** posture is diplomatically focused, with President Trump engaging in extensive consultations with regional leaders to advance a deal. However, Trump has signaled a "50/50" chance of a deal, maintaining the option to resume military action if a "good" agreement isn't reached or if Iran defaults on nuclear commitments. Secretary of Defense Hagseth is reportedly preparing rapid reaction forces for deployment to counter Iranian proxies. Former CIA Director Mike Pompeo and Republican Senators have voiced strong skepticism, warning against a deal that could empower Iran.

**Gulf States**, including Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, and Bahrain, generally support diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions, with their leaders participating in Trump's calls. Qatar's Emir explicitly affirmed support for peaceful solutions.

Among **EU members**, UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer welcomed progress but emphasized preventing an Iranian nuclear weapon and reopening Hormuz. France banned Israeli Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir from entering its territory over his actions against Gaza flotilla activists and called for EU sanctions against him.

**Russia** has undertaken a massive "revenge" attack against Ukraine, using advanced missiles and drones, underscoring its aggressive military posture in that conflict.

**China** is playing an influential, albeit indirect, role in the diplomatic efforts, with Pakistan noted as a strategic partner in this architecture.

**Turkey's** President Erdoğan spoke with Trump, expressing support for dialogue and diplomacy with Iran and offering to assist in the implementation of any agreement.

**Pakistan** is a key mediator in the Iran-US talks, with its army chief engaging in "high-level" discussions in Tehran and reporting "encouraging progress" toward a final understanding.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions persist between US and Iranian reporting on the proposed MoU. Iran explicitly denies that the nuclear issue is part of the initial agreement or that it has made any commitments regarding its highly enriched uranium, directly contradicting US reports. Similarly, while Trump implies a return to pre-war status for the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian sources strongly assert they will retain sovereign control over passage, timing, and permits. There are also conflicting accounts regarding the immediate release of frozen assets, with Iran demanding it upfront while the US suggests it will be contingent on a final nuclear deal. Unverified claims include speculative reports about the physical destruction of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's residence and the subsequent power vacuum, as well as an unconfirmed claim of five Israeli fuel tankers taking off. Propaganda is evident in Iranian state media's framing of the potential agreement as a victory for Iran's resistance and strength, often invoking historical parallels like the liberation of Khorramshahr. Reporting gaps include specific details of the "Third Imposed War" mentioned by Iranian sources, the actual content of Mojtaba Khamenei's messages, and precise demands from other regional leaders beyond general support for peace. The identity of the "Great Leader of the Revolution" whose blood is being avenged in Iranian reports is likely the recently deceased Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, while his son, Mojtaba Khamenei, is now referred to as the Supreme Leader by several sources.
